territorial_scope.description: Applies to supervisory authorities of EU Member States in cases concerning cross-border processing under the GDPR, and is binding in all Member States.

evidence.quote: where those cases concern cross-border processing

summary.short: EU regulation setting procedural rules for supervisory authorities enforcing the GDPR in cross-border cases: complaint handling, cooperation, time limits, right to be heard, access to the file and dispute resolution before the EDPB. Applies from 2 April 2027.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2025/2518 lays down procedural rules for complaint handling and investigations by supervisory authorities when enforcing the GDPR in cases concerning cross-border processing. It covers complaint admissibility (required information, a two-week period to declare a complaint inadmissible), transmission to the presumed lead supervisory authority within six weeks, optional early resolution of complaints, a simple cooperation procedure, a summary of key issues and consensus-seeking between authorities, and time limits for submitting draft decisions (15 months, or 12 months under the simple cooperation procedure, with extensions). It also sets rules for full or partial rejection of complaints with complainant input, preliminary findings and the right to be heard for parties under investigation, access to the administrative file, protection of trade secrets and confidential information, a cooperation file, dispute resolution and urgency procedures before the European Data Protection Board. It enters into force on the twentieth day after publication and applies from 2 April 2027, with transitional rules for investigations opened or complaints lodged before that date.

It does not state that it amends or repeals that regulation.

notes: Target instrument IDs are left empty for targets not known to the registry (the schema requires a string). Internal tension: Art. 36 and Art. 37(2) fix the application date at 2 April 2027, while recital 67 uses a formula of 15 months from entry into force. The text does not state the entry-into-force date, so the two cannot be reconciled from the text alone; the recital is non-operative. Entry into force is the twentieth day after publication (Art. 37(1)); the Official Journal publication date is shown on the cover as 12.12.2025 (external metadata). thresholds.note: The instrument is procedural and sets no scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation-tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty-tier or price-tier cutoffs. Its numeric provisions are procedural time limits (Arts. 4(2), 5(2), 6(3), 9(2), 10(3)-(5), 11(3)-(4), 12(1)-(6), 16(1), 19(3)-(5), 20(1), 22(2), 25(5), 27, 28(2), 29(3), 30(4)-(5), 31(1), 32(1), 33(3)), coded as events, the 15-month and 2 April 2027 application dates (Arts. 36, 37(2)) coded as events, and no fine maxima are stated. The Art. 34(1)(g) statistic on administrative fines is a reporting duty, not a threshold.
